raw_comment: In this graph, it depicts how the temperatures between the months of January and December have changed from 1850 to 2023. Generally, I noticed that as the years progress, the temperatures drastically rise. For example, in the 1940s-60s, the highest temperature between January and December was around +0.7 degrees celsius, whereas the highest temperature in 2023 was above +1.6 degrees. Each decade, the temperatures become further and further away from the average temperature of below 0 in 1850-1900. I wonder what the main cause of this rise in temperatures is and think that it may be due to climate change because greenhouse gas emissions lead to global warming. Additionally, I noticed that the temperatures for most decades are typically the highest in January, except for the 1970s and 2020s, and I wonder what the cause of this is. Also, I noticed that there is usually a drop in temperature right near December and then it rises again. This applies to my community because I have experienced global warming first hand and it is something that is very concerning for the environment. My headline for this graph would be: “How Hot Can Global Temperatures Get?”.

raw_comment:
I noticed that throughout the decades, the climate of our world has only been climbing up. Despite the incredible technological advances we have seen in this decade, it looks like there has not been a stopping point for the severe increase in temperature. Additionally, I noticed how the graph depicts the heat in each decade in a different color, each decade's color becoming more red. This noticeable stylistic choice strikes me with fascination, making me ponder about the evident climate change we are witnessing.
Why hasn't there been a sense of stability in the climate already? Especially since when you look at the previous decades, the trend of the temperatures increasing has been an evident feature of today's world for a long time so it is strange that there hasn't been a sense of regulation established already. Furthermore, with the severity of the heat depicted in the 2020 decade, I wonder if the effects of that have become even more unavoidable and clear in comparison to the other decades.
Whether it is humans, animals or plants even, we are being strongly affected by the climb in climate. We have already seen the effects on air quality, endangerment of animals, and lack of snow days. If we continue our lives oblivious to the dangerous increase in temperature, this damage will be almost impossible to reverse. 
This Decade's Hot Topic

raw_comment:
I noticed that each subsequent decade has relatively increased in temperature with the hottest decade since 1940 being 2020. Additionally, I noticed that in general, the decades and years didn't keep the regular seasonal pattern; the winters weren't always shown to be colder than the summers. This is especially true for the 2023 line where the temperature actually peaked in December. This is probably because of the seasonal flip between the northern and southern hemispheres. 

I wonder how much of this increase in temperature is from human activity and how much is the earth naturally increasing in temperature. Most likely, this large growth is from the peaking industrialization of the world, leading to more fossil fuel consumption and increased greenhouse gas release. I also wonder what could happen in the future if this trend were to continue. Would we find a solution before the earth became completely uninhabitable or insupportable to our current way of life? 

This affects my community and the whole world because if temperatures keep rising, eventually life itself will need to make a major change or risk extinction. This problem is also not isolated to the distant future because, even if the world does not completely end due to the rise in temperature, it will see a substantial shift for the worse, for example, increasing natural disasters and worse air quality.

As someone who lives in New York, I've experienced unusually high temperatures during the winter months. The daily activities within my community could also be contributing to the increase in temperatures.
 
"Turning Up the Heat Over the Decades" could be a catchy headline for this graph.

I wonder temperature increases will continue indefinitely or reach a peak, given the apparent exponential trend.

This relates to me and my community because I can anticipate the negative consequences from escalating temperatures. We are already facing these consequences with a notice in warmer summers and increased heat during the summer.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
The average global temperature has been increasing rapidly, with each year becoming hotter than the last. If the trend continues (which it most certainly will), 2024 will take the new record for hottest year. I also notice that from 1850-1900, the average temperature stayed the same, and only started fluctuating at ~1980s (fairly recently), meaning that the amount of damage global warming has on the planet is also increasing.

What do you wonder?
In January of 2016, the average temperature nearly reached the hottest temperature of 2023. What happened during this time that caused the temperature to increase so substantially? How was it able to return back to the average so quickly?

How does this relate to you and your community?
The average global temperature is swiftly increasing, meaning we aren’t doing enough to stop or even delay global warming. This graph goes to show that if we can’t come together to enact change now, there will never be a good time. It only will get harder and harder to end global warming, and the point of no return for our Earth is rapidly approaching.

Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea:
Global Warming or Humanity: Which Will End First?

This makes me worry about the weather and seasons in the future, and if the community around me will get to enjoy the outdoors as much as we used to.

raw_comment: In the graph, I noticed that the global temperature increases every decade. However, in 2023 in particular, the temperature shoots upwards in December to above +1.6 degrees celsius out of the general “grouped” temperature in the 2020s. I also noticed that in each decade, typically, January possesses a high outlier temperature (but this is different in the 2020s and the 1970s). I wonder why the 1940s-60s and 1970s average temperatures are nearly the same (with a slight increase in the 1970s). I also wonder how climate change directly affects the average temperatures in the graph, particularly with the abnormally high temperatures for 2023. I am curious if the temperatures will fall back down into the “oscillation” pattern in 2024, or will they continue to rise? The graph directly relates to my community because the rising temperatures from climate change can harm the environment and human health. If temperatures continue to rise, food production in America (and globally) can be hindered as ecosystems struggle. People can also suffer from the rising temperatures as it impacts the economy and the agriculture industry. “A Heated Topic: The Earth’s Temperatures Are Quickly Rising”

raw_comment:
I notice that average temperature of the Earth has risen drastically since the 1940s. I notice that from 1940-1970 the average temperature only slightly increased. With a maxiumum of a .8 degrees Celsius increase. However, from 1990 to 2023 the average temperature drastically increased.  The maximum increase was over 1.6 degrees Celsius. Both of these increases in temperature occurred over a 30 year period of time. Although they occurred over the same period of time they were drastically different, as the Earth has heated up significantly in the past decade. I also notice that 2023 was the hottest year ever. I wonder if the immense damage that humans have inflicted upon the Earth can be reversed as much as it needs to be. I wonder if people are too stubborn to make the changes that need to be made to salvage the Earth for future generations. As a result of this I wonder if the Earth's temperature will just continue and continue to increase until life as we know it is completely altered to the point of no return. This relates to myself and my community as I have seen the Earth getting hotter. This has been a relatively warm winter with days in the high 50s and 60s. There has been very little snow and only a few frigid days. I often wonder what the winters will be like as I grow older and if I will ever experience another winter like those that I experienced as a child.


Temperature Turmoil

raw_comment:
This graph shows temperatures throughout the past few decades (1940s-2023). The trend is each decade, temperatures are rising. The average temperature for 1850-1900 has risen 1°C since then. Temperatures in the 20s have not been exceptionally high on a global scale. This may be due to COVID and the COVID recovery years (2021-2022) because it halted many modes of transportation and slowed the economy due to a reduction in manufacturing. These factors can play a role in reducing the temperatures of the world. As we know, fossil fuels produced from transportation and manufacturing are depleting the ozone layer and causing temperatures to rise (global warming). During COVID, studies showed that the ozone layer was healing itself as a result of less carbon emissions going into the air. In 2023, the world was back in full swing. The carbon emissions probably depleted every ounce the ozone layer supposedly healed during COVID following when the restrictions were lifted. In 2023 the ozone layer probably broke down even further resulting in a rise in temperatures. I wonder why temperatures were so high in 2016. This relates to me because it is the dead of winter in NJ and this Saturday is going to be 57° Fahrenheit! This is abnormally high for a winter day in the middle of February. I predict that in future years, temperatures will continue to rise. If we do not do something major to help reduce global warming soon there will be dire consequences. 
"2023 Record High, We Might Die"

Thanks to all the students who responded.   Here are some of the catchy headlines that we received:  “It’s Only Getting Hotter: Climate Change Through the Decades” by Elizabeth of Mich.; “'How Hot Is Too Hot?” by Destii of Franklin Square N.Y.; “Are Rising Temperatures Becoming an Uphill Climb?” by Sylvia of Pewaukee High School in Wis. Please return on Friday when we will reveal the free link to the article that includes this graph. The next graph will be released by Friday, February 9.  Live-moderation will be on Wednesday, February 14 – Valentine’s Day.  The topic – changing last names when marrying.
 
Signing off – Sharon Hessney from Boston, who does what she can to not contribute to climate change, and Amy Ballard from Simpsonville, S.C., who's turning up the heat on climate change awareness.

raw_comment:
I noticed that as the decades passed, the temperature was getting higher than before, with temperatures steadily increasing since the 1970s. All years follow a certain pattern in which at the start of January the temperature richest at’s highest point, then drops, and in December it goes back up again. Before 2023, 2016 was the year with the highest temperature, but 2023 surpassed it. 2023 seems to be a weird year, as the temperature stayed comparatively low at the start of the year, and then it steadily increased and reached its highest point in December. 
I wonder what was different about 2023 than other years for it to become such a strange year?
This affects me and my community because we can directly feel the impact of it. The winter’s shorter, the summers seem hotter, and the wildlife is being affected by it. Also, as a Hondurian, the effects of climate change in Honduras are concerning as many cities are flooded more frequently and the heat is worse than before even as a tropical country. 
“Shorter Winters, Hotter Summers, We Are Getting Cooked!”

raw_comment:
This graph depicts the change in temperature on a decade scale from the 1940s to 2023, compared to the average temperature from 1850-1900. I notice that the temperature has raised to record breaking temperatures. I wonder if societal advances in innovations are what is creating the pollution causing the climb in temperature, and what the other contributing factors are. I wonder if the temperature is going to continue rising and breaking records each year, and if we can take measures to stop it. On that note, I wonder if preventative measures can even reverse the in temperatures, or if climate change has gotten so out of hand that it is irreversible. This relates to me and my community, as climate change has a negative effect on everyone, animals included. If animals that are crucial to our wellbeing are negatively impacted by climate change it can lead to many consequences, such as food security if pollinators go extinct, problems within ecosystems, and human health. 
"2023 Temperature Triumph"

raw_comment:
I notice a general increase in global temperatures by decades from the 40s to the early 80s, but a much sharper increase tat exponentially grows after the 90s up until today, indicated on such graph by a change in color, from a boring dull gray to a more vibrant yellow and dangerous red. I also notice that the highest temperature in 2000 is double that of the 40s

I wonder what factors influence changes in the increasing carbon emissions causing an increase in global temperature index. Considering that global population has also sharply spiked in such time, I wonder if that data correlates with this one and whether subsequent consumption rates are a causal factor in global emissions. 

This relates to my community as erratic weather is a grave threat to humans living anywhere, near coasts by where I live with hurricanes and floods, or in deserts with droughts and sandstorms, jungles with deforestation, or otherwise. Enviromental degradation causes mass human suffering. It must be stopped.
A catchy headline for this would be "The Looming Threat".

raw_comment:
I've seen that the temperature rose by more than 1.6 degrees Celsius in December of 2023. In addition, I see that the average temperature between 1850 and 1900 was much lower than it would be in 2023. The temperature declined between 1850 and 1900, but it only climbed in 2023. This demonstrates how the temperature has increased dramatically in recent decades. I've seen that between 1980 and 2000, the rate of temperature increase coincided with the growth of transportation and manufacturing, which increased urban pollution and contamination. 

I wonder what regulations will be required in order to stabilize Earth? How can people become more conscious of the fact that our mistreatment is the root of this problem?  

Young generations, like mine, are particularly affected by climate change since the Earth we will inherit is ruined by all the technology we have created. In an attempt to preserve the planet's deteriorating health, it will be up to us to reverse these impacts as much as possible.  

is it too late to stop the world from burning?

raw_comment:
What I notice in this graph is how every 10 years since the 1940's, the average temperature in Celsius has drastically changed.  It had first started with the average being 0 degrees celsius from 1850-1900, and now in 2023, it broke records as the hottest year and now the range is from about 1.4 to over 1.6 degrees celsius. What I wonder is how climate change is going to affect winters and summers in the years to come since temperatures have clearly been rising in an alarming way. Will they keep going up? Until what point will something drastic have to be done in order to save the planet? This relates to my community because my state has experienced many very hot summers and very cold winters so we're pretty in the middle of everything thats happening, though I do not live in a state where it's at an extreme temperature either. What's going on in this graph is it is trying to show readers how the future is starting to look. With how things are looking right now, it seems that climate change is going to have a big impact on the future and it seems that the graph is trying to show people that change has to occur now so there are no detrimental, long-lasting effects. 
Catchy phrase: Higher temperatures, Higher expectations

raw_comment:
What do you notice?

As the years increase, the temperature also increases. Most of the decades start high, experience a dip in the middle, and spike up again at the end of the decade. The temperature in each year of the decade varies a lot.

What do you wonder?

I wonder if temperatures will continuously increase or if it will plateau at some point, as the temperature seems to be increasing exponentially. I also wonder what the affects are of these increasing temperatures on the environment. I wonder if there is any way to prevent this extreme temperature increase and if anyone is already trying.

How does this relate to you and your community?

This relates to me and my community because there has to be negative affects of this drastic temperature increase throughout the years and they will most likely affect us all. My community has had noticeably warmer summers and winters, even on Long Island there was not even 5 inches of snow this past winter. There is also increasing amounts of rainstorms and flooding.

Headline:
“Hotshot sun: when will the earth become too hot to handle?”

How does this effect me and my community?


This affects me and my community because I am in an area that will get hot. 

Headline 

We are getting hotter then ever

The graph shows how the average temperature over the past few decades compares to the baseline of the average temperature from 1850 to 1900. It is shown that the temperature has been noticeably increasing every decade since the 1970s. Right now, in the 2020s, it averages about 1.6 C hotter than the baseline. It seems to be increasing exponentially.
I wonder how it will get worse, and how the changes will be shown. I've heard that as the climate becomes more erratic; more hurricanes will form and more strange weather patterns will occur, such as the major snowfall in Texas that happened a year or two ago. 
I have noticed the difference in climate in my life. The past summer was extremely hot, and many heat records were shattered around the world. Also, I've noticed a change in the winters. I feel that snowfall has become less frequent. When I was younger, there was usually one heavy snowfall in the winter. But now, there are some years when there's little to no snow at all.

This graph displays how 2023 has shattered records from past decades beginning in the early 1900s to the 1940s-60s through 2020s (present-day). I noticed that the graph included the lowest temperatures from the 1940s-60s to show that January- December is colder temperatures compared to 2023. I noticed how the rate of the average temperature has increased rapidly every 10 years since the 1940s when the increase in temperature was +0.6% C compared to 2023's increase at +1.6% C. I wonder how this could be and why have temperatures increased. The cause of the temperature increase is due to climate change or global warming which is a hot topic presently, worrying many people. This affects me and my community because I've been alive during the 2008s and 2020s period and have noticed the changes in temperatures, especially during the winter seasons since it was always colder in January compared to 2023's January.

raw_comment:
The graph depicts how temperatures have gradually increased over time, and how more recently they have skyrocketed. I noticed that 2023 had the highest temperature on record with a temperature over 1.6 degree celsius. The graph confirmed what global warming activists had feared. I'm wondering how many negative consequences will arise as a result of global warming. The ice in Antarctica has already begun to melt as a result of unusually high temperatures, as have tires in Arizona. I wonder how long it will be before we begin to see the irreversible and detrimental effects of global warming on our community. This affects my community because we live in New Jersey, where the state has imposed a ban on plastic bags  hoping to help the problem, but clearly that has not done anything seeing how 2023 had the highest temperatures ever recorded. 

Title: Greta Thunberg was right!!!!!!!

raw_comment: I notice that this graph shows temperatures throughout the years. I also notice that it gradually increases each year. As the colors get warmer is shows the temperature getting warmer too. In the earlier 1900's it is gray and mostly colder temperatures, way lower on the graph. Later 1900's to early 2000's show a yellow color and are higher on the graph but middle of the road overall in terms of temperature. The 2010's are orange and the 2020's are red, showing that the most recent years are the hottest ones in history dating pretty far back. I wonder what the cause is and what changes have happened in the world to make this big of a difference in overall temperatures each year. I also wonder if it will keep getting hotter or if the graph will one day turn gray again, or even blue. This relates to my community because I have experienced some of these years and I will continue experiencing more and seeing the changes in temperature each year. My catchy title is "Heat Waves Freaking Us Out"

raw_comment: This graph depicts the rising average temperatures per decade. As shown by the graph, the Earth's temperatures have been steadily rising since the 1940s, with 2023 being the hottest year on record. The 1940s-60s were fairly consistent, but still rising. After the 60s, the temperatures continued to increase as global warming increased. I wonder why the temperatures have spiked so significantly in 2023, with it breaking the average pattern. Global warming and climate change have become the forefront issues for the World's health, so I imagine the sudden change can be attributed to the massive increase of waste and trash that has been accumulating the last century coming to fruition. This is an important issue because it relates to every human. I remember when there would be blizzards in October and now it is lucky if we get snow by February. I have noticed the effects of global warming in my daily life now, especially in the last few years. The effects of climate change affect every part of nature, hence why it is important to notice, acknowledge, and fix global warming. A possible headline could be "Lets Turn Down the Thermostat and Take a Look at Global Warming"

raw_comment:
1. I've noticed that the average temperature has risen annually since the graph's inception. Nonetheless, there had been a significant spike in December 2023, with temperatures rising by more than 1.6 degrees Celsius. Additionally, there was a temperature increase in 2016 that brought the average temperature almost to its greatest point in 2023—it reached just over +1.6 degrees. 

2. I wonder what changes have occurred to the earth since the graph's inception? What is the cause of the increase that has occurred throughout the years? What happened in 2016 that resulted in the temperature suddenly rising?

3. This relates to my community because It is crucial to think about the reasons behind the rising temperatures and whether there is anything we can do to slow them down or stop any more abrupt changes from happening. We should protect this planet since rising temperatures have an impact on all living things on it, including us. This could lead to further problems down the road.

4. Peak Of Heat, When Is Global Warming Finally Taken Seriously?

raw_comment:
This graph depicts the increase in temperature recorded from the 1940s to 2023. From the decades recorded, it can be seen that temperatures started to steadily increase around the end of the 1970s going into the 1980s. After such, temperatures appear to climb higher and higher each decade. This leads up to 2023 being the hottest year recorded on the graph. Even though each bar indicating a temperature rise only differs in +0.2°C, these small increases are linked to grave impacts on the climate of the world. I wonder why 2016 had the most major spike in the 2010s. I understand during this year the Arctic regions experienced uncharacteristic heat and that, globally, oceans were reported to have higher temperatures than normal, resulting in international panic. I also wonder if some of this heat was normal due to natural intervals of the earth heating, but it was untimely coupled with external factors caused by society. This relates to my community because climate change is a major issue. Climate change affects everything from air quality to food. In my local community, there is a strong Environmental Commission that strives to improve the quality of the land and ultimately find ways to rally people together and fight back against climate change. No matter where you live, the negative impacts of climate change trickle in and affect all of us, even in minor ways. 

“Is It Hot In Here or Is It Just Climate Change in 2023?”

"A Melting World"

raw_comment:
From the 1850s/1900s to 2023, the average Earth temperature has increased by 2.8, or almost 3 degrees Fahrenheit. If the positive trend of temperature keeps its current speed, in a few centuries it could be something around 10 degrees warmer. That would be catastrophic to many of Earth’s diverse environments that may rely on a colder atmosphere.

We know that the Earth is heating up, and that it may continue to do so. How can we maintain our significant human progression while reducing or halting the increase of Earth’s temperature? Green Energy? Electric Cars?

The graph brings to light how significant that the last hundred years have been in the change of Earth’s temperatures. In doing so, It inspires the need for change and action. Whether that’s more recycling, use of electric vehicles, other forms of green energy, etc, working on a community and individual level is all we can do. If enough communities can do that, change will be seen.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
The average global temperature has been increasing rapidly, with each year becoming hotter than the last. If the trend continues (which it most certainly will), 2024 will take the new record for hottest year. I also notice that from 1850-1900, the average temperature stayed the same, and only started fluctuating at ~1980s (fairly recently), meaning that the amount of damage global warming has on the planet is also increasing.

What do you wonder?
In January of 2016, the average temperature nearly reached the hottest temperature of 2023. What happened during this time that caused the temperature to increase so substantially? How was it able to return back to the average so quickly?

How does this relate to you and your community?
The average global temperature is swiftly increasing, meaning we aren’t doing enough to stop or even delay global warming. This graph goes to show that if we can’t come together to enact change now, there will never be a good time. It only will get harder and harder to end global warming, and the point of no return for our Earth is rapidly approaching.

Global Warming or Humanity: Which Will End First?

raw_comment:
I notice that in December of 2023, the temperature increased by more than 1.6 degrees Celsius. I also notice that from 1850-1900, the average temperature was extremely low compared to the temperature in 2023. From 1850-1900, the temperature decreased while the temperature in 2023 only increased. This shows how the temperature has skyrocketed over the past decades. I notice how the temperature started to increase from 1980-2000 as industrialization and transportation continued developing, thus leading to more pollution and contamination in cities. 

I wonder why the temperature did not increase nor decrease from 1850-1900. What is the main factor of global warmings and how does this lead to an increase in temperature? I wonder what life would be like if fossil fuels and substances that harm the earth did not exist. By 2050, what will the world be like if the temperature keeps increasing by large amounts? 

My community and I as we are affected by global warming and high temperatures. This shows that we must save the earth and take care of it. For example, recycling and using electric cars. It will be a challenge to change our ways as we are used to using plastic water bottles and gasoline powered cars. I feel as though electric cars are expensive, but in the future if they are cheaper, I will buy one. The effect of global warming calls my community and I into action as everyone must get involved in order for the earth to be saved. 

Save the Earth: There is No Planet B

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that from the 1940s to 2023 the temperature has drastically increased at a constant rate. 2023 is at the highest temperature whereas in the 1970s, it shows the lowest. It can be stated that the temperature change is an effect of global warming.

2. I wonder why people have not talked about global warming before it became a major threat. From the graphs there is a clear change in temperature, so why is it that people are starting to get worried now when it's been a major problem for far too long. Additionally, why has no one done something to decrease this rapidly rising temperature.

3. This relates to me and my community because, while we are being affected by climate change, the whole world is. Additionally, global warming has been affecting the snow fall. During my childhood years, there was so much snow and blizzards, but now it had only snowed for 2 days throughout the whole winter.

4. A catchy headline could be, Temperatures Keep Increasing Each Year.

The reason being that water levels could rise which could lead to floods, lost of animal habitats, and increased rainfall. On the other hand, the sun has been out more in the winter which is nothing short of amazing. 
- Too Hot to Handle! Rise in Heat Making Waves!

1. I notice that the general trend of temperatures rising has been fairly linear however doesn't even begin rising until the 1970's. As of now, the highest recorded temperatures have been on the rise whereas in the past 50 years have been in their colder seasons.

2. I wonder why general trends throughout the graph suddenly stop once we get to the 2020s and we see an all-time temperature peak where it should be colder.

3. This relates to not only me and my community but the entire world as this issue has extremely lasting impacts on many no matter where they are. This global warming is expected to keep climbing and as this happens, so will many very bad complications with health, life expectancy, and food production.

4. "The snow is a no-show" The hottest we've been in history and I don't mean looks.

raw_comment:
1. I notice that over the past decades, temperatures have dangerously increased. From the 1940s to the 1980s the increase in temperature was below +1 degrees Celsius (1.8 degrees Fahrenheit) and had not been alarming. Yet, over the years from the 1990s to 2023, 2016 and 2023 stood as the hottest years surpassing more than 1.6 degrees Celsius. 
2. I wonder, what will the estimated number of natural disasters look like in the years to come. What regulations will be needed to stabilize Earth? How can people be more self-aware that this is an issue caused by our mistreatment?  
3. As the years pass by, the news on floods, wildfires, earthquakes, rise in sea levels, and the lack of fossil fuels, are more commonly heard of and experienced. This raises the tension on our safety and what is expected to come in the future.   
4. Title: Planet Earth Caught Fire, Grab The Fire Extinguisher!

This pertains to both myself and my community as we observe the tangible impacts of climate change. Winters have become milder than the norm, while summers are increasingly scorching. The temperature shift is palpable globally, impacting communities worldwide.

 

4. What's going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph's main idea.

Let's Ignite Change: It's Time to Amplify Climate Action!

1. What do you notice? If your notice makes a claim, where in the graph is the evidence to support it?
Over time, the range for the values continues to get higher and higher. 
Starting from the 1990s, the colour gets closer and closer to red to reflect how hot the temperatures are getting. 
There’s a peak in temperature in the year 2016, compared to the rest of the 2010s. 
Everything is being compared from 1850-1900. 
The temperatures were relatively stable during the 40s-60s.

How can we be sure that measurements from the 1850s-1900s are accurate? 
Is this trend something unique to our modern society, or are there swings between gradually warmer to gradually cooler temperatures?

Climate change is a big thing for young people since we will inherit a world that is damaged by all the technology that we have made. It will be up to us to undo these effects the best we can in hopes of salvaging the declining health of the Earth.

Climbing Climate 
The Hot Won’t Stop 
Damage by the Decade

Only a decade has passed, and look how much our climate has changed.

1. I notice that since 1940, global temperatures have been steadily increasing, with 2023 being the hottest year yet. The graph depicts the increase in temperature of degrees Celsius. 

 2. I wonder why people contemporarily continue to deny the prevalence of global warming and climate change when it is evident that it is in part, if not fully responsible for increasing temperatures these past decades. I wonder when governments all over the world will take proper action to mitigate human activity that causes climate problems, such as the one depicted in the graph. 

3.  This graph directly relates to my community, being the world. The influx in global temperature can have various detrimental implications: warmer ocean waters, rise in sea level, threats to agricultural systems. Such threats can pose broader threats to various occupations and people's survival. For instance, warmer global temperatures can contribute to an unpredicatable growing season for farmers, which could ultimately lead to food shortages. 

4. Hot or Not: Tracking Temperature Trends

1. I noticed that from the 1940s to 2023 the temperature has drastically increased at a constant rate. 2023 is at the highest temperature whereas in the 1970s, it shows the lowest. It can be stated that the temperature change is an effect of global warming.

3. This relates to me and my community because, while we are being affected by climate change, the whole world is. Additionally, global warming has been affecting the snow fall. During my childhood years, there was so much snow and blizzards, but now it had only snowed for 2 days throughout the whole winter.
4. A catchy headline could be, "It's too Late to Stop the Heat".

raw_comment:
I notice that there was a stable temperature range up to the 1960s, and even then, the temperature doesn't appear to rise greatly until the 1990s. I wonder if we'll ever be able to get temperatures down to pre-1990 levels again; we seemed to try in 2016, and an argument can be made that we tried a little in 2020 (as staying home led to a considerable decrease in energy consumption) but going back to "normal" seemed to make the problem even worse. 

This relates to my community because we are all affected by climate change in one way or another. We finally got our first genuine snowfall in a long time this winter, but overall, it's felt way too warm for it to be winter -- even for me, who strongly prefers being warm. 

"Things are Heating Up... Everywhere!"

 I notice that every decade the world has been getting hotter and hotter. This is presumably because of global warming. That sucks!!!! Guys. Start caring for your planet!!!
What do you wonder?
I wonder if this also has to do with the el nino and not just global warming... but I also wonder if this has to do with the polar vortex warping. Which is also because of global warming but it's a more specific reason.
How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to my community because this is the weather where I live. Personally, here in New York, it hasn't snowed in a long time. Though recently we got some snow, it wasn't enough to cause a snow day, which means it doesn't count in my eyes.
Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
Global warming weather warning!

2. I wonder if this trend will increase, or plateau in the future. I also wonder what we could do to cause this plateau.

4. "Global Disaster impending; What can we do?"

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
First, I noticed an obvious and steady increase in the average temperature since 1940. Since 1940 the average temperature has risen about 1.6 degrees celsius. I also notice the graph is made up of multiple smaller graphs showing each decade. Many of these smaller graphs have peaks in the months of January and February. Lastly, I noticed the colors of each graph are different from one another.

What do you wonder?
After looking at this graph I wonder if there is ever a point at which the average temperature will stop climbing. I also wonder what is causing this growth in temperature. Another thing I question is what are the affects of this increase and what are the things we can do to slow down or stop it? Finally, I why the graph colors are different. Is it saying gray is where we should be and red is alarming rates, or is it just to make the graph easier to read?

How does this relate to you and your community?
This graph shows average global temperatures, so it should relate to everyone on this earth, including me. Global warming has been a huge topic for awhile and it will only bigger with statistics like this. The affects of global warming can be dangerous and irreversible if we don't do anything about it. I'm only in college so this can have a big impact on my life, and possibly my kids lives. 

Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
Time to Turn Up the Heat on Climate Action.

What do you notice?
I noticed that the temperature range was constant from the 1940s through the 1960s and then the temperature started to increase.  I also noticed that there is an obvious peak temperature in the decades shown.
What do you wonder?
I wonder if the temperature will keep eventually start to level off, or maybe even start decreasing again.  Electric cars are starting to improve and sales will continue to go up.  There is also a push to employ more environmentally healthy forms of getting electricity such as solar power, wind power, and hydro power.  I wonder if these will continue to grow and later enforced by the government. 
How does this relate to you and your community?

This trend of increasing temperature could eventually be irreversible so we need to be aware of how to slow it down until we can eventually stop and reverse it.

raw_comment:
I notice two trends on the graph: first, the average temperature increases by about .2 degrees Celsius every decade; second, the range of temperatures on average increases every decade. The exceptions to this trend are the 1970s where the average temperature does not change significantly from the previous decade, and the 1980s where the range of temperatures is significantly smaller than the 1940s-1970s.

I wonder why the two outliers exist and what triggered these decades to have unexpected rangers and average temperatures. I wonder why despite evidence many do not believe the dangers global warming presents. I wonder where these temperatures were taken and if that has any impact on the data trend. I wonder why 2023 was significantly warmer than other years in the 2020s. I wonder if it’s possible to reverse this trend and prevent global warming.

Global warming relates to my community for numerous reasons but one of the most notable are potholes. The toll wide temperature ranges have on infrastructure is obvious. When roads, bridges, and most other substances get cold they contract. The problem lies when the temperature rapidly increases; the asphalt expands irregularly forming cracks and aiding in the formation of the infamous pothole. This chunk of missing road causes thousands of dollars in damages annually when any unassuming driver hits one.

The Dangers We Pose to Ourselves

raw_comment:
1) I've noticed that there's been a great jump in the average temperature in Celsius since the 1850s-1900s. As of 2023, the average temperature has gone up over 1.6 degrees Celcius. After the 1970s, the temperature graphs seem to rise by at least 0.2 Celcius per decade. The only year that even comes close to matching the temperature of 2023 is 2016.
2) I wonder if the rising temperatures result from a natural process or if man and man-made inventions have affected them. One specific thing I wonder is if the common use of cars has caused rising temperatures. Cars started becoming common means of travel around the 1950s, and the first big jump in temperature we see is in the 1970s. I wonder if the evolution of cars and the automobile industry could have impacted the temperatures this significantly. Overall, I'm just curious about how any of our factories, nuclear plants, etc. could have contributed to the rising temperatures.
3) This relates to me and my community because it means a change in our environment. This winter, we've seen much less snow than average, considering our first big snowfall wasn't until January. When I was younger, we would start getting our first snowfall in October. Since the temperature is changing around us, we have to adapt to the hotter weather during all seasons. Not only do we as people need to adapt, but so does the ecosystem.
4) Rising Temperatures: Earth or Inferno?

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that the world is getting progressively hotter. Based on the graph, it looks like the world will keep heating up for years to come. It shows no signs of slowing down. There was a temperature spike in the 1970’s yet the line for 2023 is still much steeper. 
2. Is there a way to slow down the heat? Is there a specific issue that is the main cause of the heat increase? I wonder which countries and cities the temperatures are being measured from, especially since it may be hard to access global records of temperatures from the 40s and 50s. Will it ever be too hot to be outside?
3. This graph relates to me and my community because we have to endure these heat increases every summer. It adjusts our living conditions in terms of price and what we can do outside. For winter, we experience much more rain instead of snow and that also changes our living conditions.
4. Burning Up: Will There Be a Solution For Global Warming Before It's Too Late?

raw_comment:
Relations? 
Looking at this graph from a modern perspective, the response will automatically be global warming. The world is warming, that is a fact. However, what’s causing it? In the 1940s-1970s the temperatures remained fairly constant. But, this was the era of large industrialization, planes and automobiles. For the first time, the average citizen had a car. So, why has the increase in temperature been so significant in modern times? Times that people are so very conscious of carbon emissions? If the argument is that climate change is caused by cars (hence the need for electric cars), then why would an era with such a focus on automobiles have such a low temperature? Were the emissions not happening? Do the emissions accumulate? If they accumulate, then why was the temperature seemingly not impacted by the emissions of the Industrial Revolution? Older cars typically use a carburetor or don’t have a catalytic converter- thus having the potential to use even more gas, and more emissions. So what’s going on here? The earth’s natural cycle? 

Title: 
It’s Gettin’ Hot In Here- The Temperature Results of the Last Century

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that there has been a steady increase in temperatures each decade from the 1940s to the 2020s. Some people believe that global warming is fake, but the data clearly shows that temps have been on the rise. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder where in the world this data was taken. It appears that the warmer temperatures occur during our winter here in the US and the colder temperatures occur during our summer. I think the data was taken in the Southern Hemisphere. This leads me to wonder if different parts of the world experience global warming differently; could North America’s temperature changes be more or less drastic than those of our southern hemisphere friends?

How does this relate to you and your community?
Here in Michigan, it gets quite scorching in the summer; so much so that we often have to cancel tennis matches and practices because of an unbearable heat index on the courts. With these rising temperatures, it’s only a matter of time before we will be forced to play indoors year-round.

Catchy headline: You’re not the only one experiencing hot flashes; the Earth is heating up too!

raw_comment:
1) I notice that temperatures have gradually increased globally since the 1850s-1900s rising to a total of over 1.6 degrees Celsius warmer in 2023, pointing to continued temperature rises in coming years. I noticed that the 1940s-1960s and 1970s had similar temperature graphs up until the end of the 1970s when the temperature spikes increased. I noticed that 2023 has one of the steepest temperature increases compared to the years surrounding it. 

2) I wonder if the graph has the 1850s-1900s as the basepoint of the graph because that is when the Industrial Revolution was taking place worldwide. I wonder if the expansion of industrialization and the increased use of fossil fuels over time catalyzed this serious temperature increase. I wonder why certain years have big spikes in temperature increase and then the years following drop back down to a more constant temperature increase. I wonder what can be done to mitigate the effects of these global temperature rises and what measures can be put into place. 

3) This relates to me and my community because these temperature increases have had the effect of making summers much more uncomfortable and increasing air conditioning bills for all in addition. My community has noticed that our winters have become less cold and the main precipitation that we see up until January is rain instead of snow. 

4) Rising Global Temperatures: Are They Really Temporary

raw_comment:
According to the EUCCCS, since the 1960s Earth’s average temperature has steadily increased each year. At the start of 2023, the average temperature was at an all time high, with the high and low January temperatures being close to 1.8 and 1.05 degrees above the average temperature in 1960, respectively.  Between 1940 and 1960 the temperatures followed very similar trends - almost indistinguishable from each other - which makes me wonder what happened in the 1970s to cause such a spike in temperatures. In the 1970s, oil production was at an all time high and America began the steep climb of industrialization, helped by the development of steam powered vehicles. However, this was only in America. What happened in the rest of the world to spike such change in Global temperatures? An increase in global temperature is detrimental to life all over the world. Since many plants and animals are not accustomed to these changed temperatures, they will be forced to adapt or die off. Thus, if global temperatures continue along their current trend, much of life may not be able to persist in the future, affecting all future generations. Furthermore, intense heat in arid climates will dry out the soil, making it infertile to farming and therefore taking away possible food sources. Our current generation’s grandchildren and possibly even children will not be able to experience the beauty of Earth as we have.

"Earth's Fever: Global Temperatures on the Rise, Burning Up Like Never Before"

raw_comment:
This graph exhibits a severe problem many see threatening our future generations.  
 I notice that the graph seems to be misleading because although it looks as if the temperatures have risen exponentially over the years; temperatures have only risen .8 Celsius.
I wonder why people seem to be fearful of recent temperatures, there have been many warm and cold years throughout history, so I believe the rising temperatures are not as severe as many see. I also wonder if eventually, the earth will begin to drop temperatures in the coming years.  I wonder if humans actually do promote the warm temperatures as much as people say.
This relates to my community because the winter we saw in Michigan was nothing near average.  We saw many warmer days, but in January there was a massive cold front that crossed the US, resulting in below 0 temperatures.  Although temperatures seem to be rising, they might not be as severe as many say, and many believe there will be colder years ahead.
"Global warming, natural or man made?"

raw_comment:
1. Mean global temperature has been rising by nearly a fifth of a degree every decade since the 1970s. With this change in average temperature comes an increase in variation as well. These changes all amounted to 2023 being the warmest year on record, and by a lot. If this trend continues we will reach the warned +2 degrees celsius sooner than many people realize. 

2. I wonder why temperature didn’t have nearly as much change before the 1970s. The change seemed to happen very quickly as well which I find to be strange when talking about rising global temperatures. I also wonder why 2023’s average temperature started increasing so far before other years that allowed it to become the hottest year by such a large margin. Finally, I wonder whether the large increase in temperature stems from human actions, or if it is naturally occurring. 

3. Climate change is something that relates to my community and all other communities around the globe. Changing temperatures pose threats to much of the wildlife and activities that me and my friends love to do. I even notice now that we get less snow each year for skiing, one of my favorite things to do in the winter. While I think increasing temperatures are already prevalent in my community, it will only increase in prevalence as temperatures become more extreme. 

4. Rapidly Increasing Temperatures: Naturally Occurring or Human Actions?

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that following the 1940s, the global temperatures have risen dramatically- more than 1 degree celsius. Additionally, there was a big jump in the temperatures from the 1980s to the 1990s. I also notice that in 2023, the increase in temperature was dramatic compared to the previous years. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder if the increase in temperature has something to do with how industrialized the United States has become in the last 80 years. With an increase in industrialization and mechanization, the carbon emissions would additionally increase. Also, the rise in the automobile production/industry might have something to do with the increase in temperature.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This could possibly relate to my community because we depend on cars to get to and from school, work, and other extracurricular activities. Using the car too much would lead to more vapors being released from the cars fuel system- aka an increase in carbon emissions. Also, there might be some factories nearby that emit tons of carbon into the atmosphere which is not good.

The Rise in temperature recently raising dramatically

raw_comment:
1) I notice that our planet is getting hotter, and 2023 is no different. However, in 2023, the planet rose to average temperatures never seen before. I also notice that although there have been some spikes in average temperature throughout history, rarely is there a year with a constant trend upward like 2023 had (for the most part). 
2) I wonder what, if anything, can be done to stop this problem before the damage to our planet worsens. This seems like a major problem that the average person can't do much to help, however, is there something that we could be doing to hopefully stop or slow global warming? 
3) This relates to me and my community because we can see the effects of global warming this winter. When normally we would have a snowy, cold January, all the snow that has fallen this year has been melted by the unusual rain mixed with unusually high temperatures. This graph reflects what we are seeing in our community and makes us worried about the future of our planet. 
4) My Headline: Is Earth Becoming an Oven?

I also think that this led to some realization by the general population because, in the 90s, there were initiatives taken to protect the environment, such as the “Save the Rainforests” movement. 


What do you wonder? One thing I wonder is if there is going to be a way to lower temperatures back down to what they were in the 1940s-60s or even the '80s or '90s. Is it only gonna get hotter until the end of the world, or will people be able to fix this decades-long mess we’ve created? 


How does this relate to you and your community? It relates to me because I grew up in a time when there was always something about climate change being talked about. As for my community, however, I’m not quite sure. I know that climate change is affecting everything, but I think that because it was so gradual over the decades people have mainly ignored it, only paying attention to it when it seems disastrous.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I noticed that there was not much temperature change in the 1940s through the 1970s. This may be from the amount of factories or pollution in the air, I also noticed that the 1940s-60s had a lot of lines in that section compared to the other decades. The lines represent the average temperature and I think there are more lines because that section measures 3 decades instead of one. I found it interesting that the creator of this graph sought to include all three of those decades instead of just starting at the 1960s. 
What do you wonder?
I wonder what began in the 1980s that caused the temperature to make a significant incline which then caused a trend of every decade since then. Was it the inventions or the number of factories being used that caused more pollution and global warming? Or was it something else that caused it?
How does this relate to you or your community?
This relates to me because I noticed that in 2023 summer was unusually warm and I knew that temperatures were rising. Also living in Michigan everyone has been noticing that there is seldom any snow anymore until January. I know that my community has been annoyed by this and we all miss when we had guaranteed snow instead of just hoping to get some snow by chance. 
Catchy Headline.
Is Earth Becoming The Sun?

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
There is a clear upward trend in temperature throughout the decades. However, I also noticed that the title is a bit misleading. It uses the word "shattered", which immediately makes me think there was a huge surge in temperature. After looking at the graph, the average was only a measly 0.1 degrees Celsius more.

What do you wonder?
I wonder why there is an increase in temperature over time. Did humans cause it? Is it a natural cycle of the Earth? My guess, because there is a very minimal change in temperature through decades, is that this is a natural cycle of the Earth.

How does this relate to you and your community?
Realistically, this doesn't bother or relate to me much. Yes, there is a slow increase of about a Celsius in temperature. However, it is not large enough of an increase for me to feel it physically or worry about it at all. To summarize, this doesn't relate to me or my community enough to say anything definitive.
